newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec and Newfoundland to talk on Churhill Falls.
newsitem.headline: Quebec and Newfoundland to talk on Churhill Falls.

text.p: Newfoundland said on Friday that it expects to begin talks with Quebec on possibly renegotiationg the hydroelectric power contract between Hydro-Quebec and Churhill Falls (Labrador) Corp.
In a press release, Newfoundland Premier Brian Tobin said officials for both provincial governments have been discussing parameters for potential talks on the contentious contract.
At issue is the long-term contract in which Churchill Falls sells roughly 30 billion kilowatt hours of power a year to Hydro-Quebec.
"There have been three discussions at the officials level during the past week to explore the parameters for a potential negotiation between our two provinces," Tobin said.

Tobin issued the statement from Bangkok, where he and Quebec Premier Lucien Bouchard were participating in a trade mission of provincial premiers led by Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien. Further discussions on Churhill Falls would be held in Canada, Tobin said

Last autumn, Tobin complained that Newfoundland will soon begin losing money on the contract, which runs to 2041. The 5,420 megawatt Churhill Falls facility sells the bulk of its output to Hydro-Quebec.

Hydro-Quebec is a significant exporter of hydroelectric power to the northeastern United States, and late last year agreed to open its network so that other private and public utilities can transport power to customers outside Quebec.

Quebec government-owned Hydro-Quebec has been vigorously defending the Churhill Falls contract. Under the contract, which was negotiated in the early 1970s before the spike in world energy prices, the price paid by Hydro-Quebec declines over time.
